name: Nimitz-class aircraft carrier
role: Nuclear-powered aircraft carrier: the base for a carrier air wing of strike fighters, airborne early warning, electronic attack and helicopters

serviceWindow.statusNotes: USS Nimitz was commissioned on 3 May 1975 and was scheduled to leave service in 2026: she left Bremerton on 7 March 2026 for a homeport shift to Norfolk ahead of inactivation. On 14 March 2026 the Navy extended her service to March 2027 to hold the carrier fleet at 11 until USS John F. Kennedy (CVN 79) is delivered (s3). She was in service on 2026-03-15. The original plan to leave service in 2026 is from s4.

dimensions.crew: about 3,200 ship's company plus about 2,480 air wing

propulsionSummary: Two A4W nuclear reactors drive four shafts through steam turbines, which gives the ship unlimited range and about 20 to 25 years between refuelings.

weapons.name: RIM-7 Sea Sparrow
weapons.mountSummary: Two launchers of eight missiles each (s1). The Navy fact file lists the Sea Sparrow range as classified, so the 19 km engine range is estimated.

weapons.name: Mk 15 Phalanx CIWS
weapons.mountSummary: 20 mm six-barrel gun. FAS lists Phalanx range as classified, so range and round count are estimated.

sensors.name: AN/SPS-48E 3D air search radar
sensors.role: Gives range, bearing and height on air targets

sensors.name: AN/SPS-49(V)5 air search radar
sensors.role: Long-range 2D air search, FAS gives its range as 250 nautical miles

sensors.name: AN/SPQ-9B surface and low-air radar
sensors.role: Fast scan for sea-skimming missiles and boats near the ship

sensors.name: AN/SLQ-32A(V)4 electronic support
sensors.role: Detects, identifies and bears on hostile radars

sensors.name: Bridge and flight deck lookouts
sensors.role: Eyes and binoculars from the island and flight deck

radar.note: A 333 m hull with a large island, a crowded flight deck and parked aircraft is among the biggest radar targets in any fleet.

infrared.note: Steam turbines driven by reactors do not put out a gas-turbine exhaust plume, but the hull and flight deck are large and warm.

acoustic.note: Four shafts and 97,000 tons of displacement make a loud contact, and aircraft operations add noise.

visual.note: A 4.5 acre flight deck and a seven-story island can be seen from far off on a clear day.

brief.whatItIs: The Nimitz class is the US Navy's workhorse aircraft carrier. USS Nimitz, the lead ship, is 333 m long, displaces about 97,000 tons and carries an air wing of about 85 aircraft: strike fighters, early-warning aircraft, electronic attack jets and helicopters. Two nuclear reactors give it effectively unlimited range.
brief.howItIsUsed: A commander uses the carrier as a mobile airbase and the centre of a strike group. The air wing does the fighting: fighters shoot down aircraft, strike aircraft hit ships and shore targets, and the E-2 early-warning aircraft sees farther than any ship radar. The carrier itself carries only close-in defences (Sea Sparrow, Phalanx, chaff and an electronic warfare suite), so cruisers and destroyers must ring it and carry the long-range air and missile defence. It can launch about four aircraft a minute from its four catapults. Its weakness is that a hit on the flight deck or hangar can stop air operations, and if the carrier is damaged the whole group loses its main weapon. Keep it away from submarines and out of reach of saturating missile salvos.
typicalMissions: Air superiority and strike from the sea
Anti-surface and anti-submarine warfare through the air wing
